name: x265 (HEVC)
summary: x265 is the reference open-source HEVC/H.265 encoder from MulticoreWare. It is mature and very configurable, encodes 8, 10 and 12-bit with 4:0:0/4:2:0/4:2:2/4:4:4, and has first-class HDR10, HLG and Dolby Vision signaling, and its output plays on almost every modern device at 10-bit. Weaknesses: it is far slower than hardware HEVC, its defaults are tuned for low bitrates (SAO and psy settings often need adjusting for high-fidelity work), its efficiency trails modern AV1 and VVC encoders, and this build lacks SCC, alpha and MV-HEVC (those options are rejected). HDR10+ works only in 10-bit encodes (see the hdr section).

hdr.summary: For HDR10: encode 10-bit 4:2:0 (-D 10, --profile main10), signal BT.2020 primaries, PQ transfer and BT.2020 non-constant matrix (--colorprim bt2020 --transfer smpte2084 --colormatrix bt2020nc, --range limited), and copy the source's static metadata with --master-display and --max-cll. Those two imply --hdr10, which in turn turns on --repeat-headers. Add --hdr10-opt for PQ-aware QP (10-bit 4:2:0 only). For HLG: same primaries/matrix with --transfer arib-std-b67 and no mastering metadata needed. --video-signal-type-preset BT2100_PQ_YCC[:volume] sets the whole VUI in one go. 12-bit PQ (Main12) is valid HEVC for archival masters, but it is not HDR10 and most consumer decoders can't play it. Dolby Vision (--dolby-vision-profile plus --dolby-vision-rpu) needs 10-bit 4:2:0 and VBV; the help lists profiles 5, 8.1 and 8.2, and this build also accepts 8.4 (verified). HDR10+: --dhdr10-info <json> is not in the help, but in this Homebrew build it works for 10-bit encodes only (the 10-bit library is compiled with HDR10_PLUS; verified with a hdr10plus_tool JSON). At 8-bit and 12-bit it is ignored with a warning, so for those depths inject the metadata afterwards with hdr10plus_tool.
hdr.example: x265 --input src.y4m --y4m --output out.hevc --preset slow --crf 18 --output-depth 10 --profile main10 --range limited --colorprim bt2020 --transfer smpte2084 --colormatrix bt2020nc --master-display "G(13250,34500)B(7500,3000)R(34000,16000)WP(15635,16450)L(10000000,50)" --max-cll "1000,400" --hdr10 --hdr10-opt --repeat-headers
pitfalls: --master-display order is G, B, R, WP, then L(max,min). Chromaticity is in 0.00002 units (ffprobe's x/50000 numerator); luminance is in 0.0001 nits (1000 nits = 10000000). Swapping max and min is a common mistake.

--hdr10-opt does nothing at 12-bit or without BT.2020/PQ signaling: x265 4.3 logs an error ('Recommended Settings for HDR10-opt ...'), disables it and keeps encoding with exit code 0, so check the log (verified on this build).

HDR10+ depends on bit depth in this Homebrew build. --dhdr10-info is not in the help, yet a 10-bit encode (-D 10) accepts it and writes SMPTE 2094-40 SEI on every frame; the 8-bit and 12-bit libraries print '--dhdr10-info disabled. Enable HDR10_PLUS in cmake.' and ignore it (all verified on 4.3+1). A malformed JSON makes the 10-bit encode abort. For 8/12-bit, or to add metadata later, use `hdr10plus_tool inject -i out.hevc -j metadata.json -o out_hdr10plus.hevc`.

Dolby Vision through x265 is Main10 only (12-bit is refused: "profile - 5, profile - 8.1, profile - 8.2 and profile - 8.4 are Main10 only") and needs --vbv-bufsize/--vbv-maxrate (verified error messages); profile 8.1 also needs --master-display. A 12-bit archival encode cannot carry DV.

The RPU or HDR10+ JSON must match the encoded frames one-to-one. Trimming, --seek/--frames, frame-rate conversion, interpolation or --frame-dup break the match. A frame-interpolating pipeline needs regenerated metadata (general practice; not spelled out in the tool READMEs read).
x265 only signals color; it never converts. The input must already be PQ/HLG BT.2020 at the right range.
--max-cll 0,0 means 'unknown'. After grading or tone changes the source's MaxCLL/MaxFALL may no longer be correct.
--hdr-opt is the deprecated old name of --hdr10-opt; older guides (including the codecalamity article) still show hdr-opt=1.

Through ffmpeg, pass HDR settings in -x265-params with ':' separators and use commas inside values (max-cll=1000,400). The HDR article warns that ffmpeg did not carry HDR metadata over automatically in the versions it tested; verify the output with ffprobe or MediaInfo. HDR10+ also passes through this way (dhdr10-info=metadata.json inside -x265-params with -pix_fmt yuv420p10le; verified with ffmpeg's libx265 on this machine).
Pasted curly quotes break the --master-display string; some shells also need the parentheses quoted.
--video-signal-type-preset overrides individual VUI flags; its BT2020_YCC_NCL row in the help lists colormatrix bt709, which looks like a help-text mistake.
--tune grain disables AQ; --hdr10-opt is documented to work best with AQ enabled.

presets.notes: CTU 32, min CU 16, 1 ref, dia search, subme 0, no SAO, no AQ, no weighted prediction, rd 2, scene cut off. Largest files; the wiki calls it inconsistent. Previews only.
Like ultrafast but min CU 8, hex search, scene cut on, sign hiding on. Previews and throwaway encodes.
CTU 64, 2 refs, AQ mode 2, SAO and weightp on, 15-frame lookahead. Quick drafts.
As veryfast with subme 2. Real-time-ish encodes on strong CPUs. Lumora's fastest HEVC rung (measured about 1.6x medium's speed, 7% larger).
3 refs; early skip off. Not on Lumora's ladder: on an M3 Max it was slower than medium (CPU time) and about 3% larger. The anime guide advises against fast for anime.
Default: 3 refs, hex, subme 2, b-adapt 2, rd 3, 20-frame lookahead, b-intra on. psy-rdoq has no effect here (rdoq-level 0).
star search, subme 3, 4 refs, rect on, rd 4, rdoq-level 2, psy-rdoq 1.0, 25-frame lookahead. Lumora's default rung; the anime guide's recommended preset; a common good balance.
8 B-frames, 5 refs, rect+amp, rd 6, TU depth 3, weightb, 40-frame lookahead, limit-tu 4. A common archival choice.
As slower but max-merge 5, no ref/mode limits, no limit-tu. One guide's archival starting point; small gains over slower.
merange 92, subme 5, TU depth 4, 60-frame lookahead, tskip on, rskip off. The wiki says it is slightly worse than veryslow in practice; not worth the time.

rateControl.notes: Default (28). Constant perceived quality, variable size. Best choice for archives and files. Lower = better; about +6 halves size (wiki).
CRF with a peak-rate cap for streaming or device limits. VBV makes output non-deterministic unless --const-vbv. Required shape for Dolby Vision encodes.
Fixed quantizer with I/P/B offsets from --ipratio/--pbratio. Wastes bits versus CRF; for testing only. QP 0 is not lossless.
Hits an average bitrate without lookahead knowledge; less efficient and consistent than CRF (wiki).
Accurate file-size targeting. --slow-firstpass (default) keeps pass 1 accurate; --multi-pass-opt-analysis/-distortion can refine pass 2.
Constant bitrate for broadcast/streaming; --strict-cbr keeps the average within about 5%.
Experimental capped-CRF that plans per keyframe segment; forces closed, fixed GOPs.
Bit-exact; rate control ignored. The wiki recommends x264 for lossless instead because it is much faster.

options.description: Where the encoded stream is written. x265 writes a raw Annex-B HEVC elementary stream, not a container; mux it with mkvmerge, MP4Box or ffmpeg afterwards.

options.description: Bit depth of the encoded stream, which is also the depth x265 works at internally. 10 gives Main10; 12 gives Main12 and needs a build with 12-bit support.

effect.size: ± (10-bit is often smaller at equal quality than 8-bit)

recommendations.why: The guide found 10-bit gave better results than 12-bit at the CRF values typically used for anime.
HDR10 output needs a 10-bit pipeline; the article had a commenter whose encode came out 8-bit until -D 10 was given.

options.lumora: encoders.json x265.args: `--output-depth {bits}`; the HEVC 12-bit recipe (Codec.hevc12) passes 12.
options.notes: If omitted but --profile is set, x265 derives the depth from the profile. Hardware decoders for Main12 are rare (most TVs, phones and streaming boxes decode Main10 at most), so 12-bit is mainly an archival/master format. Dolby Vision is refused at 12-bit (verified on this build: 'Main10 only').

options.description: Binary RPU file (one Dolby Vision metadata unit per frame, as written by dovi_tool extract-rpu). x265 interleaves each RPU into the matching access unit.

recommendations.why: dovi_tool extracts the RPU from the source stream; the alternative is to encode plain HDR10 and add the RPU later with `dovi_tool inject-rpu`.

options.notes: CLI only. The RPU must line up frame-for-frame with what x265 encodes; trimming, --seek, --frames or frame-rate changes break the alignment. (Alignment requirement is general practice; the dovi_tool README page read did not spell it out.)

options.description: Text file of user SEI messages to insert, one per line as `<POC> <PREFIX> <NAL type>/<SEI type> <payload>`.
options.notes: Docs say only prefix SEI is supported.

options.description: Stops after encoding this many frames.
options.notes: Also used as a hint for rate control and still-picture detection when the frame count is known.

options.description: Skips this many frames at the start of the input before encoding.
Declares the input as separate fields in temporal order (top- or bottom-field first). x265 then codes fields as pictures and signals it in SEI.
options.notes: Docs also accept 0/1/2. Give field size and field rate. Deinterlacing or IVTC before encoding is usually preferable for archival. Listed only in `--fullhelp`, which Lumora's flag probe reads.

options.description: Enables field coding for interlaced input.
Uses a higher-quality dithered downconversion when the input has more bits than the encode (for example 16-bit input to an 8-bit encode).
options.notes: Only matters when input depth exceeds internal depth. CLI only. Listed only in `--fullhelp`, which Lumora's flag probe reads.

options.description: Library behavior: whether x265 copies each input picture. Turning it off saves memory copies but the caller must keep buffers valid until encoded.
options.notes: Only meaningful for API users; leave alone on the CLI.

options.description: Computes and reports SSIM between source and reconstruction.
options.notes: Reporting only. For a metric-optimized encode, --tune ssim changes encoding decisions instead.

options.description: Computes and reports PSNR between source and reconstruction.
options.notes: Reporting only. PSNR rewards blur, so pair with --tune psnr only for benchmarking.

options.values: main, main10, mainstillpicture (help); docs list main12, main422-10, main444-12, -intra variants etc.
options.description: Enforces the limits of an HEVC profile and signals it. For 12-bit 4:2:0 use main12; for 4:2:2 10-bit main422-10.
options.lumora: encoders.json x265.args: `--profile {x265_profile}` (main12 for the 12-bit recipe).
options.notes: Help only lists three names, but the docs list the full RExt set: main, main-intra, mainstillpicture/msp, main444-8, main444-intra, main444-stillpicture, main10, main10-intra, main422-10, main422-10-intra, main444-10, main444-10-intra, main12, main12-intra, main422-12, main422-12-intra, main444-12, main444-12-intra. -intra is signaled automatically when keyint is 0 or 1. CLI only.

options.description: Requests a minimum decoder level. x265 adjusts references, CTU size and VBV to stay inside it, or aborts if it can't.
options.notes: With CRF and a level, x265 forces VBV on, and VBV makes output non-deterministic (verified message in this build). Levels 5.0+ require CTU 32 or larger.

options.description: With --level-idc, allows the High tier bitrate limits of that level instead of Main tier.
Constrains the encode toward UHD Blu-ray rules: high tier, closed GOP, no temporal layering, 1080p or 2160p only.
options.notes: Docs call it highly experimental; it switches itself off if other options conflict. Messages in this build: 'Supported resolutions are 1920x1080 and 3840x2160', 'Turning off open GOP'.

options.description: Lets x265 write a stream whose profile/level is NONE instead of aborting, for example with too many references or a tiny CTU.
options.notes: Such streams may not play on hardware decoders. Avoid for archives meant to be playable.

options.values: <integer,...> per NUMA node; '-' none, '+' one thread per core (help); '*' all remaining (docs)
options.default: not stated (docs: all threads on all nodes)
options.description: Sets the thread-pool size per NUMA node. On a single-socket machine one number is simply the worker-thread count.
options.lumora: encoders.json x265.args: `--pools {threads}`. On Apple silicon (one NUMA node) a single number caps the worker threads, which is how Lumora limits CPU use.
options.notes: Quote values containing + or * in the shell. Ignored if every pool-using feature (WPP, lookahead slices, threaded-me) is off.

options.description: How many frames are encoded at once. More frame threads speed things up with a small efficiency loss because later frames can't fully use not-yet-finished references.

recommendations.why: The guide found 1 gives the best quality on small CPUs and saw identical results from 2 to 16.
The wiki reports frame threading costs roughly 1-3% efficiency for a large speed gain, with no difference between 2 and 16 threads in 4.1.

options.notes: Sources agree the loss is small; they differ on whether 1 is worth the slowdown.

options.description: Wavefront parallel processing: encodes CTU rows in a staggered order so several rows run at once. About 1% efficiency cost for several times the parallelism.

recommendations.why: The wiki recommends keeping it on unless an external chunked encoder supplies parallelism.

options.notes: Disabled automatically for tiny frames or without a thread pool.

options.description: Splits each frame into this many full-width slices that are coded independently.
options.notes: Docs call it experimental and suggest it only when frame threads and WPP can't keep the CPU busy.

options.description: Parallel mode analysis across CU candidates.
options.notes: Deprecated from release 4.1 per the help text. Leave off.

options.description: Parallel motion estimation across references/partitions.
options.notes: Deprecated from release 4.1 per the help text. Leave off.

options.description: Runs CTU-level motion estimation in its own thread pool. Aimed at many-core, low-clock servers.
options.notes: New in 4.2 (experimental). Docs: switched off automatically with fewer than 32 cores, without a pool, or with VBV. Little use on a Mac.

options.description: Overrides CPU feature detection for SIMD. --no-asm runs plain C code.
options.notes: Forcing features the CPU lacks can crash. Only for debugging.

options.values: ultrafast, superfast, veryfast, faster, fast, medium, slow, slower, veryslow, placebo
options.description: Sets a bundle of search and analysis options from fastest/largest to slowest/smallest. Options you set explicitly always override the preset.

The guide calls slow the best quality-per-time trade for anime and advises against fast.

recommendations.why: The wiki says placebo performs slightly worse than veryslow and ultrafast is inconsistent.

options.lumora: encoders.json x265.preset default 'slow'; Codec.hevc12 rungs fast, medium, slow, slower, veryslow, placebo with seed speeds 1.0/0.55/0.25/0.09/0.045/0.012.
options.notes: Lumora's speed/saving seeds are its own estimates, not from these sources. See 'presets' for what each one changes.

options.values: psnr, ssim, grain, zerolatency, fastdecode (help); animation also accepted
options.description: Applies a content- or goal-specific adjustment on top of the preset.

Lowers psy-rd and aq-strength to 0.4, sets deblock 1:1 and adds 2 B-frames.

recommendations.value: avoid grain tune on slower presets
recommendations.why: The anime guide warns tune grain is too strong when combined with slower presets; it prefers manual psy settings.

An unknown tune aborts with 'preset or tune unrecognized'. The library also contains a 'vmaf' tune name, which changed nothing in this build.

options.description: Largest coding block size. Bigger blocks code flat areas and high resolutions more cheaply.

recommendations.why: The guide keeps the default.
Dropping to 32 cost roughly 1-2% in the guide's anime tests.

options.description: Smallest coding block size. Larger minimums are faster but lose fine detail.

recommendations.why: The guide recommends the default.

options.notes: Docs list 32, 16, 8 as valid; help also prints 64.

options.description: How many extra transform splits are tried inside intra blocks.

options.description: How many extra transform splits are tried inside inter blocks.

options.description: Pushes mode decisions toward keeping the source's visual energy (texture, grain, sharpness) rather than the mathematically closest smooth result.

Part of the grain tune.
The docs note lower bitrates call for lower psy strength or motion can judder.

recommendations.why: The guide's usual range.

Part of the grain tune.

options.notes: Order is G, B, R, then white point. Chromaticity units are 0.00002; luminance units are 0.0001 cd/m2 (so 1000 nits = 10000000). Quote the string in the shell. The help's color-volume presets use min 5 or 50 (0.0005/0.005 nits) and L(10000000,1) for BT2100x108n0005.

options.description: Content light level SEI: MaxCLL (brightest pixel) and MaxFALL (brightest frame average), in nits.

recommendations.value: copy from source, e.g. 1000,400; 0,0 if unknown

options.notes: If Lumora changes brightness (tone/look edits), the source values may no longer be accurate.

options.description: One option that sets primaries, transfer, matrix, range and chroma location together, optionally with a standard mastering-display volume.

recommendations.why: The HDR article enables it so HDR headers are present throughout.

Writes a decoded-picture hash SEI so a decoder can check it reconstructs frames exactly.

options.description: Writes the alternative transfer characteristics SEI naming a preferred transfer curve, which some HLG delivery specs use.

recommendations.value: 18 (arib-std-b67 / HLG), only if your delivery spec asks for it
recommendations.why: The docs say this SEI is required for HLG signaling; 18 is the transfer code for arib-std-b67 in the HEVC transfer table.

Unsure which approach a given player expects. Some HLG workflows pair this SEI with a bt2020-10 VUI transfer for backward compatibility; that pairing is not described in the x265 docs (unverified).

options.notes: Docs say it is needed for HLG signaling (alongside --atc-sei). See HEVC spec D.3.3.

options.notes: Added in 3.6; frame-parallel since 4.2, reworked in 4.3. Applied to every GOP regardless of noise unless --selective-mcstf. Removes grain, so avoid it when grain should be kept.

Boolean flags take =1/=0, and no- forms work as keys. Keys missing from the x265 help still work here if the library supports them; for example dhdr10-info=<json> adds HDR10+ in 10-bit encodes (verified).

options.notes: ffmpeg libx265 wrapper option (FFmpeg 9.0.2), not an x265 CLI flag. Not described in the FFmpeg codec docs page read; behavior inferred from the option text. Subject to x265's DV rules (10-bit 4:2:0, VBV).

recipes.name: HEVC 12-bit archival, live action
recipes.why: Slower preset with low CRF; SAO off and gentler deblocking keep fine texture at low CRF; intra smoothing off for sharp sources; deeper references and lookahead. Keeps the default AQ mode and cutree where the guides disagree.

recipes.name: Anime, 10-bit, high quality
recipes.why: The anime guide's high-quality line: dark-scene AQ against banding, limited SAO near CRF 18-20, and 8 B-frames for a few percent saving.

recipes.name: Anime, 12-bit archival (Lumora-style)
recipes.why: Combines tune animation (low psy-rd and aq-strength) with gentler deblocking and limited SAO. Note --tune animation is accepted but not in the help list. The anime guide found 10-bit better than 12-bit at high CRF, so 12-bit is only worthwhile at low CRF.

recipes.name: Heavy film grain
recipes.why: The grain tune keeps QP flat (rc-grain, qpstep 1, ipratio 1.1, pbratio 1.0), turns off AQ, cutree and SAO, and raises psy-rd/psy-rdoq so grain doesn't smear or pulse. The anime guide finds it too strong on slower presets; the manual alternative is psy-rdoq 2-3 with --no-sao and --deblock -2:-2.

recipes.name: HDR10, 10-bit (playable)
recipes.args: --preset slow --crf 18 --output-depth 10 --profile main10 --range limited --colorprim bt2020 --transfer smpte2084 --colormatrix bt2020nc --master-display "G(13250,34500)B(7500,3000)R(34000,16000)WP(15635,16450)L(10000000,50)" --max-cll "1000,400" --hdr10 --hdr10-opt --repeat-headers
recipes.why: Full HDR10 signaling with static metadata copied from the source; hdr10-opt applies PQ-aware QP at 10-bit. Replace master-display and max-cll with the source's values.

recipes.name: HDR PQ, 12-bit archival master
recipes.args: --preset slower --crf 14 --output-depth 12 --profile main12 --range limited --colorprim bt2020 --transfer smpte2084 --colormatrix bt2020nc --master-display "<from source>" --max-cll "<from source>" --hdr10 --repeat-headers --no-sao --deblock -2:-2
recipes.why: Keeps more precision than HDR10 for later re-encodes. Leaves out --hdr10-opt (disabled at 12-bit) and Dolby Vision (refused at 12-bit). Most TVs won't decode Main12; make a 10-bit HDR10 copy for playback.

recipes.name: Dolby Vision profile 8.1 re-encode
recipes.args: dovi_tool -m 2 extract-rpu src.hevc -o RPU.bin ; x265 --input src.y4m --y4m --output out.hevc --preset slow --crf 18 --output-depth 10 --profile main10 --colorprim bt2020 --transfer smpte2084 --colormatrix bt2020nc --master-display "<from source>" --max-cll "<from source>" --dolby-vision-profile 8.1 --dolby-vision-rpu RPU.bin --vbv-bufsize 160000 --vbv-maxrate 160000 --repeat-headers
recipes.why: dovi_tool mode 2 makes the RPU profile 8.1 compatible. x265 refuses Dolby Vision without VBV and refuses 8.1 without --master-display (both verified on this build). The VBV numbers are placeholders: choose values your target level and devices allow. Frames must stay identical to the source.

recipes.name: HDR10+ (10-bit in-encode, or post-injection)
recipes.args: hdr10plus_tool extract src.hevc -o metadata.json ; x265 <HDR10 args> --output-depth 10 --dhdr10-info metadata.json --output out.hevc  (for 8/12-bit: x265 <HDR10 args> --output out.hevc ; hdr10plus_tool inject -i out.hevc -j metadata.json -o out_hdr10plus.hevc)
recipes.why: In this build --dhdr10-info works only in 10-bit encodes (verified: a JSON extracted with hdr10plus_tool round-trips through x265 -D 10 with one 2094-40 SEI per frame). At 8/12-bit it is ignored, so inject afterwards. Either way the JSON must have one entry per encoded frame.

recipes.name: HLG broadcast-style
recipes.why: The preset sets BT.2020 primaries, ARIB STD-B67 transfer, bt2020nc matrix, limited range and chroma location 2. HLG needs no mastering metadata. Some delivery specs also want --atc-sei/--pic-struct.

recipes.name: Two-pass size target for streaming
recipes.why: Two passes hit an exact average; VBV caps peaks for streaming devices.

recipes.name: ffmpeg HDR10 via libx265
recipes.args: ffmpeg -i in.mkv -map 0:v:0 -c:v libx265 -pix_fmt yuv420p10le -preset slow -crf 18 -x265-params "colorprim=bt2020:transfer=smpte2084:colormatrix=bt2020nc:range=limited:master-display=G(13250,34500)B(7500,3000)R(34000,16000)WP(15635,16450)L(10000000,50):max-cll=1000,400:hdr10=1:hdr10-opt=1:repeat-headers=1" out.mkv
recipes.why: x265 options pass through -x265-params with ':' separators; the pixel format sets the bit depth.

recipes.name: Fast preview encode
recipes.why: veryfast is the fastest preset that keeps AQ and SAO; good for checking a pipeline before a long archival run.
